rules: Bugs: every new bug found by the suites (N1-N8, F1-F8, A1-A6 and the other mods' 17) and every known bug the engine suites reproduce fully or partly, plus the two JS-only known bugs the report discusses (Autopilot KB4, Fun Facts KB8). Not included: bugs not reproduced, passing regression guards (Fun Facts KB10-13, Autopilot #12-#35), Autopilot KB31 (Hardened's own bug), Autopilot KB10 (not reproduced: the mechanism tried fails only on the engine, an engine divergence; the original and the page pass), Nicknames KB3 (Black Pyramid 0.4's own save bug, fixed in BP 1.x), Elite Few EF-KB8 (Clever Recruiter 2.1.6's bug, fixed in 2.1.8), heal_repair_fix's outdated README.

caught: a test in `tests` fails on the bug in that env (on the open bug, or for a fixed one on the old code: `regression.failed_before`, from FOUND_BUGS.md / TEST_APPROACHES.md); a launch that dies before its test reports counts as a failure (boot bugs).
reachable: a fixed bug's regression test runs there but wasn't run on the old code; for bugs without tests (none now) and for mocks, an estimate that the approach reaches what the bug needs.
no: every test of the bug skips there (reason in `why`), or the tests pass there on an open bug (tried, doesn't reproduce).

mocks: caught only if an existing mock test fails on it (fun_facts/mocktests, autopilot/mocktests, nicknames/test.nut, other mods' test.nut); otherwise reachable only for needs=logic, or where a unit-level mock test exists but wasn't run on the old release.

code, engine, jsdom, ui: derived by coverage_update.py from a `bbtest.py --env all` run of every suite (statuses.json, skips.json); see `date`. jsdom is the engine with the real page in jsdom (`--env jsdom`), ui the engine with it in headless Chromium (`--env ui`).

tests: the scenario tests (file::test as bbtest.py prints them) that reproduce the bug, from the mods' FOUND_BUGS.md / KNOWN_BUGS.md; controls (vanilla, without the mod) left out. regression (fixed bugs): failed_before — envs where the test failed on the old code; old_zip — the released versions it was verified against, if any.

needs: the most demanding thing the bug needs to show up: logic (pure functions, data in, data out), data (game scripts and data off the maps: hiring, events, items, boot), save (save/load), battle (a tactical battle), world (world map, locations, simulation), ui (the mods' JS), thirdparty (Legends, Reforged, Hardened or another third-party mod).

status (the three main mods only, after the 2026-11-12 fixes in the working tree): open, fixed (in the working tree, or in a release for the regressions), not-a-bug, investigated (looked into, not changed). The coverage bars count every bug whatever its status.
